body:
_Migrated from issue #1341, filed 2026-08-03._

Three defects in the `Reader.tsx` bookmark-save retry added in #1321, found by the pre-release refuter loop for v4.1.29. None corrupt data — the route is replace-on-write and idempotent, every chain terminates, and the correct CFI is always sent — so they did not block that tag. Filing so they are tracked rather than remembered.

### 1. The retry timer is not cleared when `.finally` starts a coalesced send (MED)

`frontend/src/pages/Reader.tsx` ~308-332. `.catch` runs before `.finally`. When a coalesce is pending, `.catch` arms `saveTimer.current` with backoff, then `.finally` calls `flushCfiSave()` **immediately, with no backoff**, leaving that timer armed. Two independent save drivers then coexist — the state the single-flight design exists to prevent. The exhaustion branch also resets `saveRetries.current = 0` just before `.finally` starts a fresh chain.

The documented contract (comment at ~52-55) is "three attempts over ~14s". A virtual-clock simulation of the real functions, two page turns then no further input:

| per-request latency | sends | span |
|---|---|---|
| 1500 ms | 4 | 19 s |
| 6000 ms | 8 | 59 s |
| 25000 ms | 8 | 157 s |
| 30000 ms | 8 | 225 s |

The slow rows are the realistic ones: `cps/ub.py` builds the app.db engine with `connect_args={'timeout': 30}` and sets `PRAGMA busy_timeout=5000`, so `database is locked` blocks 5-30s **before** raising — the regime this retry exists for. The verification in #1321 used a fault that failed instantly, which is the 1500 ms row, so it never exercised it.

Fix is likely one line: clear `saveTimer.current` before the coalesced `flushCfiSave()`.

### 2. Retries and the assertive announcement outlive the reader (MED, accessibility)

No mount guard anywhere in the file (`isMounted` / `AbortController` / `mountedRef` → zero matches). The effect cleanup clears `saveTimer.current` at the instant of unmount, but a retry scheduled *afterwards* by a still-settling `mutateAsync` is never cancelled, and `flushCfiSave` never checks whether it is still mounted.

Close the reader while a save is in flight and later fails: further POSTs continue for minutes, then

```js
announce(t('Could not save your reading position.'), { assertive: true });
```

`AnnouncerProvider` sits above the router, so it is still mounted. A screen-reader user gets an `aria-live="assertive"` interruption about the reader while on the book-detail or library page, potentially minutes after leaving it.

Note the `mutateAsync`-over-`mutate` choice was deliberate so the bookkeeping survives unmount. It does; nothing stops it.

### 3. Retry timer callback leaves a dead id (LOW)

The timer callback is bare `flushCfiSave`, unlike the debounce path which nulls `saveTimer.current` first. After a retry fires, `saveTimer.current` holds a dead id, so the cleanup's `if (saveTimer.current)` is truthy and sends a redundant keepalive beacon on close with nothing pending.

### Related, pre-existing — not introduced by #1321

The unmount keepalive beacon is issued outside the `saveInFlight` guard, so it can overlap an in-flight save. Simulated with a slow-but-**successful** save (ordinary contention that clears inside the busy timeout): the beacon carrying page 2 lands at t=1280, the save carrying page 1 lands at t=20800, and the server ends on page 1 while the user last read page 2. No retry fires, because nothing failed. Reaching it needs only: turn a page, turn another within 800 ms, close the reader, during contention.

This code is byte-identical to pre-#1321, so it is not a regression — but `CHANGES-vs-upstream.md` states "At most one request exists at a time" and "0 overlapping requests", which is not true of the close-the-reader path. That row should be narrowed to the retry loop it actually describes.

### Test gap behind all of it

#1321 added no frontend tests. The two "client half" tests are Python regex source-pins over the `.tsx` text asserting `"mutateAsync" in flush`, `".finally(" in flush`, and that the `saveInFlight` assignments appear. All of them still pass under every defect above. By the project's own anti-slop bar — "a source-pin that only checks a field name appears is not a test" — that is coverage theater for the half of the change carrying the risk. The fix should land with real vitest/RTL coverage driving fake timers through the retry path.
title: Reader save-retry: coalesced re-entry races the armed retry timer, and retries outlive the reader
